prerequisites: Familiarity with concepts associated with functions (domain, range).
Basic knowledge of set theory and relations.
Technological branch baccalaureate formation is sufficient.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to understand and master the basic concepts of discrete mathematics and their application to solving engineering problems.
Express a real situation or problem using a graph.
Construct Eulerian and Hamiltonian paths in the corresponding graphs.
Utilize trees and their properties as a data structure.
Solve real problems using graph theory.
Construct a finite automaton recognizing a given simple language and describe the regular language associated with a small given finite automaton.
Relate regular languages with regular expressions and equivalent automata.
Recognize the limits of languages that can be recognized by finite automata.
Describe some application of finite automata.
Construct simple grammars generating a given language and determine the language generated by a grammar.
Simplify a given context-free grammar and transform it into any of the normal forms.
Recognize context-free languages and know their formal properties.
Describe some application of context-free grammars.
Design a simple Turing Machine associated with a given language.
Reproduce Chomsky's hierarchy related to formal languages.

syllabus_topics: Concepts of graphs and their representation
Non-deterministic Finite Automata (NFA) and their equivalence with DFAs
NFA with lambda-transitions (NFA-λ) and their equivalence with NFAs
Regular Expressions (RE) and their equivalence with Finite Automata
Regular grammars and their equivalence with Finite Automata
Introduction to lexical and syntactic analysis in compilers
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as (0.90 x ((T1 + T2 + T3) / 3)) + (0.10 x CL), provided all minimums are met. A minimum of 4 out of 10 points is required for T1, T2, and T3. If minimums are not met, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. In the extraordinary call, evaluation consists of a single theoretical exam divided into three parts (TE1, TE2, TE3), each requiring a minimum of 4 out of 10. The final grade is (TE1 + TE2 + TE3) / 3 if minimums are met, otherwise the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0.
